newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open mostly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open mostly unchanged.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open mostly unchanged Tuesday, based on market orders at 1018 EDT, traders said.

NYCE's weekly spec/hedge report showed the speculators to be holding a 21.3 percent net long position, a sharp increase from the previous week. Market analysts expect the report to prompt liquidation during the session, with nearby support in December pegged at 76.10 cents a lb.
"This could be negative for the market, and the (USDA crop) condition report had a farily good increase in the crop condition," Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes, said.
Monday, USDA said 56 percent of the cotton crop was in good to excellent condition, compared with 54 percent the previous week.

Still, the development of the U.S. cotton remains about two weeks behind schedule due to planting delays early in the season, and cold, wet weather during the early stages of growth, industry sources said.
Three percent of the U.S. cotton crop was in very poor condition and 10 percent was in poor condition, the USDA said.
Monday, the benchmark contract closed down 0.28 cent at 77.12 cents after trading from 77.39 to 76.75 cents. The rest settled 0.18 lower to 0.05 cent firmer.
An estimated 7,500 lots changed hands on the day.
Resistance in December remained at 77.70 to 77.95 cents.
Traders expect volume to remain thin as many players have extended Friday's Fourth of July holiday.
NYCE said 25 notices were issued today, bringing the total number of notices to date to 756.
